title: Tenant fanout guardrail and rolling upgrade safety for private control planes
creator: Elena Gomez
body:
Summary:
We need a protection layer for the private/dedicated control plane that prevents a single tenant or a tenant upgrade from fanouting traffic and causing cross-tenant instability during upgrades or partial region failures. This ticket implements a "fanout guardrail" (admission + tokenized circuit-breakers), an SLO-aware rolling-upgrade strategy, and explicit load-shedding rules for tenants on Dedicated/Private deployments.

Background and motivation:
- Recent postmortem of INC-2026-01 showed a tenant-triggered control-plane storm during a rolling upgrade which amplified API fanout and exhausted routing agents in one region. Impact: several tenants experienced increased tail latencies and failed requests for 12 minutes.
- Existing isolation relies on coarse admission limits and node-level eviction; we lack a tenant-scoped fanout cap and SLO-driven rollback/rollback-safety for private control planes.
- Customers running Private deployments expect that control-plane upgrades and tenant traffic spikes won't cascade across other tenants.

Goals / Non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Implement tenant-scoped fanout caps (requests per second to downstream serving clusters) enforced at the control-plane ingress layer.
  - Add tokenized circuit-breakers that track cross-tenant resource consumption and can trip preemptively when error budgets deplete.
  - Define SLOs for control-plane operations (API success-rate, median/95/99 latency for management APIs) and wire those into rollout/upgrade automation to allow automatic pause/rollback.
  - Implement deterministic load-shedding policies per tenant with fallbacks (graceful degrade: reduced parallelism, queueing with retry-after, prioritized control-plane requests).
- Non-goals:
  - Re-architecting the serving runtime itself (this focuses on control-plane admission and upgrade safety).

Proposed approach and design decisions:
1) Tenant fanout guardrail (enforcement point: ingress router/service mesh):
   - Maintain a tenant metadata table with per-tenant max_fanout (RPS to downstream pools) and burst allowance. Default conservative values for private deployments; customers can tune via console.
   - Implement token bucket check at control-plane ingress that counts downstream fanout tokens; tokens requested per ephemeral request based on worst-case expansion factor (e.g., for broadcast or batch-to-many operations).
   - If token request exceeds budget, apply graceful downgrade: prioritize critical control-plane operations (e.g., health checks, config reads) and reject lower-priority ops with clear error codes and Retry-After header.
   - Rationale: stopping fanout upstream prevents downstream node thrash and supports safer upgrades.

2) Tokenized circuit-breakers tied to error budgets and SLOs:
   - Circuit state machine keyed by tenant+region with states: CLOSED, SOFT_OPEN, HARD_OPEN.
   - Transition triggers: sliding-window error budget burn rate (from SLO exporter), downstream latency spike thresholds, and infrastructure pressure signals (e.g., routing-agent queue length > X).
   - Soft open: reduce fanout cap by configurable fraction and enter short cooldown; Hard open: deny expansion requests and route traffic to fallback model variant or region.
   - Persist circuit decisions for audit and to help automated rollbacks.

3) SLOs and rollout automation integration:
   - Define control-plane SLOs: 99.9% control-plane API success, p95 latency < 120ms, p99 < 400ms for management API. Also define tenant-facing SLOs impacted by control plane (e.g., provisioning latency).
   - The upgrade orchestrator will poll SLO metrics during canary windows. If canary or cumulative error budget burn exceeds threshold, orchestrator pauses and initiates a staged rollback.
   - Rollout cadence: per-region canary of N tenants chosen by tenancy score (mix of small/large), then staggered by tenant_score windows with minimum observation windows (e.g., 15m canaries).

4) Load-shedding policy and priority classes:
   - Introduce request priority classes: SYSTEM, CONTROL_HIGH, CONTROL_LOW, USER_API. In overload, CONTROL_LOW and USER_API can be shed first.
   - Implement per-tenant queued windows with backpressure signaling to SDKs (Retry-After), and an explicit reject code for ephemeral denial.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- Fanout guardrail enforces per-tenant downstream RPS caps in integration tests and prevents >90% of previously seen fanout spikes in replay tests (see synthetic workload replay in GCS).
- Tokenized circuit-breaker state transitions exercised in unit and e2e tests; metrics emitted for each state change and writing to audit log.
- Upgrade orchestrator halts and rolls back in simulation when SLO burn exceeds threshold; test harness simulates canary failure and validates pause/rollback.
- Load-shedding produces Retry-After and uses correct priority ordering under controlled overload in staging cluster.

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Week 1 (Spike): implement prototype token bucket integration at ingress + unit tests. Deliverable: prototype PR and benchmark numbers. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2289)
- Week 2: circuit-breaker state machine + SLO integration + metrics exporters. Deliverable: design doc and PR. (Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/Fanout+Guardrail+Design)
- Week 3: load-shedding priority classes + retries + SDK backpressure behavior. Deliverable: SDK change doc and PR. (SDK PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/147)
- Week 4: e2e tests, staged rollout automation, and canary policy wiring. Deliverable: staging runbook + dashboards. (Dashboard: grafana.redwood.ai/d/private-controlplane/fanout-guardrail)

Monitoring, metrics, and dashboards:
- New metrics: tenant_fanout_tokens{tenant,region,state}, circuit_state_transitions{tenant,region,from,to}, controlplane_api_p95/p99, tenant_error_budget_burn_rate.
- Dashboards: per-region tenant top-10 fanout contributors, canary health panel, rollback triggers panel. Alert: when >3 tenants hit HARD_OPEN in 5m -> Pager.

Testing and validation:
- Load replay harness using logs from INC-2026-01 to reproduce fanout; validate guardrail prevents cascade.
- Chaos testing: simulate routing-agent node failures and ensure load-shedding and circuit breakers protect non-impacted tenants.
- Security review: ensure circuit states and audit logs do not leak tenant secrets; encryption for audit trail required.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Conservative default caps vs. customer experience: conservative caps reduce blast radius but may break legitimate spikes. Mitigation: configurable per-tenant policies and a soft-open grace period.
- Complexity vs. operability: tokenized circuit-breakers add state and telemetry overhead; we will start with a light-weight in-memory state replicated to etcd and only persist events for audit.
- Interaction with Dedicated autoscaler: ensure guardrail signals can be throttled by autoscaler rather than hard-deny when capacity is available.

Review feedback (summary of early design review on 2026-02-18):
- PM (Jordan Li): make the default policy opt-in for existing customers; offer a migration path.
- Security (Priya Sharma): require HSM/KMS protection for persisted circuit events in Private.
- SRE (Marcus Chen): increase observation window for p99 triggers to avoid false positives from transient GC pauses.
- Design (Maya Ortiz): surface clear UX in Console explaining the Retry-After error and how to upgrade tenant allowances.

Follow-ups / next tickets to create after merge:
- ENG-63080: Admin Console controls for per-tenant fanout tuning and audit history.
- ENG-63099: Autoscaler integration with soft-open feedback loop.
- ENG-63120: Post-deployment runbook and customer communications templates.

Next steps (this week):
- Finish prototype PR, add unit tests for token accounting (Ravi).
- Schedule security review with Priya and request HSM KMS gating for audit events (Elena).
- Prepare canary tenant selection heuristic and staging runbook (SRE).

Comments and timeline updates:
- 2026-02-11 (Elena): Prototype shows ~30% CPU overhead in ingress proxy when tracking tokens for top-100 tenants; exploring sampling for low-volume tenants.
- 2026-02-15 (Ravi): Implemented state machine and basic metrics emission; pushing PR for early feedback. PR link above.
- 2026-02-22 (Marcus): Ran chaos test; guardrail prevented fanout cascade but caused a spike in user-facing 429s for the misbehaving tenant — acceptable trade-off but we need clearer client-side guidance.
- 2026-03-02 (Elena): Security review scheduled for 2026-03-05. Will update ticket with review outcome.

Acceptance and sign-off checklist (to be signed in comments):
- [ ] Design doc reviewed and approved by SRE and Security
- [ ] Unit & integration tests added with high coverage
- [ ] Staging rollout executed with synthetic replay and chaos results attached
- [ ] Console controls wired for per-tenant overrides
- [ ] Runbook and customer communications drafted

Assignee note: prioritize the prototype and state machine telemetry this sprint. If we find excessive ingress overhead, move to sampled accounting + estimated downstream multiplier for low-volume tenants.
